input.quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale: There is a minimum commitment on us — Section 5(a) sets monthly floor fees ("not less than $____ per month") for Hosting and Support Services, referred to again as the "minimum monthly fees" in the documentation/disputes clause (p0047). It sits at the fallback, not the preferred position, so we do not redline it. (1) Commitment period: the Agreement runs for an initial 1-year term and renews only in successive one-year periods, with either party able to give notice of non-renewal 30 days before year end (p0078), so the commitment never extends beyond the current 12-month term. (2) Exit: Section 14 gives us an unconditional election to terminate — TrueLink continues services only "until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement" (p0079) — so the floor fees can be shed at will with roughly a month's notice; this is a minor variance from the fallback's clean 30-day reduction right (the effective date can fall up to ~60 days out) and we note it rather than flag it. (3) No shortfall penalty, liquidated damages or early-termination charge exists anywhere in the document; the floor is a monthly fee only, so nothing punitive needs converting to a true-up. This is therefore not walk-away territory (no multi-year take-or-pay without exit), and the minimums are in any event unfilled blanks to be completed commercially. Separately, the credit-report ordering obligation in Section 3(i) applies only where we voluntarily route an underwriting request through the Interface, and Section 2(a) expressly leaves us free to use alternative systems, so it is not a minimum purchase or volume commitment; the storage and bandwidth figures in Section 3(a)/(c) are service specifications, not usage caps with penalties.
